html:
Fascist Italy's invasion and conquest of the Ethiopian Empire, launched in October 1935. It was the last great colonial war of conquest in Africa and a blow that helped wreck the League of Nations.

Benito Mussolini wanted an empire and revenge for Italy's defeat at the Battle of Adwa in 1896. After a clash at the wells of Walwal in 1934, Italian armies invaded from Eritrea in the north and Italian Somaliland in the south. They had tanks and aircraft, and they sprayed mustard gas on soldiers and villages, against the treaties Italy had signed.

The League of Nations named Italy the aggressor but its sanctions were weak and left out oil. Addis Ababa fell on 5 May 1936. Emperor Haile Selassie went into exile and spoke to the League in Geneva, warning that what happened to Ethiopia would happen to others. Italy joined Ethiopia, Eritrea and Somaliland as Italian East Africa. Ethiopian resistance fighters kept up a guerrilla war, and Italian reprisals killed many thousands.

In 1941 British and Ethiopian forces drove the Italians out and Haile Selassie returned. The war roused Black protest worldwide and fed Pan-Africanism. Italy carried the Obelisk of Axum to Rome in 1937; it came home only in 2005. In 1960 Abebe Bikila won the Olympic marathon barefoot in Rome.
sum: Fascist Italy's invasion and conquest of the Ethiopian Empire, launched in October 1935. It was the last great colonial war of conquest in Africa and a blow that helped wreck the League of Nations.
